2.evidence_source: Here, we examined the psychometric properties of BAS-2 scores in Poland for several reasons.
2._section_summary: The Introduction outlines the rationale for examining the psychometric properties of the 10-item Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) in Poland, noting sociocultural change and a lack of prior research in Polish men. The authors predict a unidimensional factor structure (to be tested using EFA and CFA), measurement invariance across sex, lower scores in women, and convergent validity including a negative association with BMI. The section does not provide sample sizes, participant demographics, survey method, or actual correlation statistics.

3.evidence_source: “Data from the first subsample were used to examine the factor structure of the BAS-2 ... Data from the second subsample were used to examine the fit of a one-factor model of BAS-2 scores ...”
3._section_summary: This section describes two subsamples (both Polish and White) used in the paper: the first subsample (N = 336; 171 women; M age = 34.95) used for exploratory factor analysis of BAS-2, and the second subsample (N = 385; 212 women; M age = 35.38) used for confirmatory analyses and validity checks. BMI (self-reported) means are reported for both subsamples (M = 24.31 and M = 23.91). The section does not specify survey method, education levels, recruitment source, or correlations between BAS-2 and BMI.

4.evidence_source: APolish translation ofthe BAS-2 (Tylka &Wood-Barcalow, 2015) was used (see Appendix for link to online Supplementary Materials).
4._section_summary: This section reports the measure used to assess body appreciation: a Polish translation of the BAS-2 (Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015), consisting of 10 items rated on a 5-point scale from 1 (Never) to 5 (Always). The section does not mention any study numbering (e.g., 'Study 1') or multiple sample subsets, nor does it provide sample characteristics, BMI assessment, or correlations with BMI.

5.evidence_source: 'The BAS-2 was translated into Polish by three professional translators.'
5._section_summary: This section describes translation and back-translation procedures for the BAS-2 and a study to assess item and score equivalence in a bilingual group of English Studies Master's degree students (53 women, 17 men). Data were collected in January–February 2017 via anonymous paper-and-pencil questionnaires administered by research assistants; correlations between English and Polish item scores ranged .69–.90 and Pearson's correlation between total scores was .95. The section also notes that the first subsample completed only the BAS-2 while the second subsample completed all measures.

6.evidence_source: A two-stage factor analytic approach was adopted to examine the factor structure of the BAS-2.
6._section_summary: This section describes the statistical analyses used to evaluate the Polish BAS-2, including a two-stage factor analytic approach with separate analyses for a first and second subsample, and testing measurement invariance across men and women. It reports use of principal-axis factor analysis and CFA (AMOS v.22), fit indices (CFI, RMSEA, SRMR, -2 statistics), Cronbach's alpha for internal consistency, independent-samples t-test to compare genders, and Pearson correlations with BMI and other constructs for convergent validity. The text explicitly mentions analyses on a first subsample and a second subsample but does not label separate studies.

7.evidence_source: "There were no missing data in BAS-2 scores."
7._section_summary: This preliminary analyses section reports that BAS-2 scores had no missing data and other variables had at most 0.5% missingness (Little's MCAR test non-significant). The authors examined normality and found skewness/kurtosis within limits; the two subsamples did not differ significantly in sex, age, or BMI. The section refers to 'both subsamples' but does not provide sample sizes, demographic percentages, or correlations between BAS-2 and BMI.

8.evidence_source: The one-factor structure of BAS-2 scores in the second subsample had unacceptable model fit: -2(35) = 184.993, p < .001, -2 normed = 5.286, CFI = .947, RMSEA= .106 with 90% CI = .091 – .121, SRMR = .038.
8._section_summary: This section reports confirmatory factor analysis results for BAS-2 in a 'second subsample', noting an initially unacceptable one-factor model fit which improved after adding specified error covariances. Reliability was excellent (Cronbach's alpha = .94 overall; .95 for men, .93 for women) and factor loadings ranged from .61 to .88.

9.evidence_source: There was no significant between-group difference in total BAS-2 scores, t(383) = 0.04, p = .970, d < 0.01, M_{\text{men}} = 3.72, SD = 0.81, M_{\text{women}} = 3.72, SD = 0.73.
9._section_summary: This section reports measurement invariance across sex for a one-dimensional model using MGCFA, finding configural, metric, and full scalar invariance. A t-test comparing total BAS-2 scores between men and women showed no significant difference (t(383) = 0.04, p = .970), with identical mean BAS-2 scores for men and women (M = 3.72) and reported SDs of 0.81 (men) and 0.73 (women).

10.evidence_source: Text: 'There was no significant between-group difference in total BAS-2 scores, t(383) = 0.04, p = .970, d < 0.01, M_men = 3.72, SD = 0.81, M_women = 3.72, SD = 0.73.'
10._extracted_caption: Table 1 Measurement invariance across sex from the second subsample.
10._section_summary: This section reports measurement invariance across sex (men vs. women) using MGCFA (see Table 1) on the second subsample. Group sizes are Men (n = 173) and Women (n = 212); configural, metric, and scalar invariance were supported and mean BAS-2 scores did not differ between sexes (M_men = 3.72, SD = 0.81; M_women = 3.72, SD = 0.73; t(383) = 0.04, p = .970).

11.evidence_source: Table 2 caption: '...Pearson correlation coefficients between BAS-2 scores and scores on all other measures from the second subsample.'

11._section_summary: The section reports measurement invariance testing across sex for a one-dimensional BAS-2 model, finding configural, metric, and full scalar invariance which permitted mean comparisons. A t-test comparing men and women on total BAS-2 scores found no significant difference (t(383) = 0.04, p = .970; M_men = 3.72, SD = 0.81; M_women = 3.72, SD = 0.73). Table 2 (second subsample) shows mean BMI and correlations with BAS-2 (All = -0.20; Men = -0.32; Women = -0.14).

12.evidence_source: The Polish BAS-2 scores showed good convergent validity (Table 2).
12._section_summary: This convergent validity section reports that the Polish BAS-2 demonstrated good convergent validity. For the whole sample and separately for men and women, BAS-2 (body appreciation) correlated positively with self-esteem, body-related hubristic and authentic pride, positive affect, and positive orientation, and was significantly negatively associated with body-related shame, body-related guilt, and BMI. The section references Table 2 and notes gender-separated analyses but does not report sample size, demographics, or numeric correlation coefficients.
